name: scry
description: SessionStart checks that tell an agent session the true state of the world and establish that repository Markdown is untrusted historical material. Also installs PreToolUse hooks that deny a tool call: one denies any dispatch that names no model — a subagent or workflow agent (a blank model silently inherits the session's, which is how a week of premium allowance can go in one session) and a metered agent CLI run through Bash (with no -m flag the CLI's own config default answers, which is how a month's budget went in one night) — and one denies a first attempt at an expensive Elixir force-rebuild. It also warns once, before it happens, when a headless `claude -p` run would bill the API account instead of the subscription. Plus an advisory on first contact with a large, actively-worked source file. A SubagentStart hook tells a spawned subagent, and only when it is true, that the worktree it was handed is behind origin/main and how far — SessionStart context never reaches a subagent, so an agent otherwise greps a stale tree and reports missing what merely is not checked out. A PostToolUse advisory notes, once per file, when a session writes a Markdown file this repo's conventions do not expect, and that scratch Markdown may be cleared out at session end. A Stop hook reports once per session what the session is leaving behind: how many finished build worktrees are still on disk and what they occupy, and the untracked Markdown files written since the session started. It names the cleanup command, lists the files, and deletes nothing. Available on demand via /scry. A PreToolUse ADVISORY speaks when a Bash command creates a branch without naming a start point, giving how far HEAD sits behind origin/<default> and how old the last fetch is, since a count measured against a stale remote-tracking ref is itself stale; SCRY_BRANCH_POINT_FETCH_HOURS (default 2) sets when a fetch counts as dated. It never fetches, moves nothing, and denies nothing. A plugin monitor (Claude only) watches when the session's prompt cache goes cold — read from the status-line payload, the only place Claude Code reports it, via a small wrapper the user points statusLine at once — and, at most once per user message, asks the session to write a handoff while the cache is still warm; a UserPromptSubmit hook is what re-arms it, so tool calls, cache hits, and the handoff itself never do. SCRY_CACHE_HANDOFF=0 disables it; SCRY_CACHE_HANDOFF_LEAD_SECONDS (default 120) sets how long before expiry it speaks. The same status-line wrapper shows the cache at the end of the bar: minutes until it goes cold, and the size of the re-read the next request pays once it has. After /clear, the SessionStart fleet check names the session just left (id, title, resume command) and prints the handoff written for it, if any — the live-window rule otherwise hid exactly that session.
